passage: Childminder's note, Tuesday afternoon. Baby Chinmay started crying when his rattle rolled away. Thomas, two, who had been busy with blocks, looked over, picked up the rattle, walked across and held it out. He patted Chinmay's head twice. Chinmay stopped crying. I said quietly, "You helped your brother feel better, Thomas," and left it there. Yesterday Thomas would not share his blocks, and I did not bring that up. 🙂

qa.q: What did Thomas do with the rattle?
qa.a: Thomas picked up the rattle, walked across and held it out to Chinmay, then patted his head twice.

qa.q: What might Thomas have been feeling when he saw Chinmay crying?
qa.a: He may have felt concern for his brother, since he stopped his block play, brought the rattle and patted him.

qa.q: Why did the childminder only name the kindness quietly and not ask Thomas to repeat it?
qa.a: Empathy grows better when it is noticed warmly than when it is demanded every time, and Thomas is still very young.

qa.q: How did Chinmay experience the moment?
qa.a: Chinmay was comforted, since his crying stopped once his rattle was back and his brother's hand patted his head.

grounding: Shows an older toddler handing a toy to his crying baby brother and patting him, and a caregiver quietly naming the empathy.

passage:
In the kitchen in Lisbon, baby Yonas started to cry. Abebe, two, stopped playing, looked at him, and carried over his own toy giraffe.

He pushed it into Yonas's hands and patted his head. "There."

Their mother, Sofia, knelt beside them. "Abebe, you saw Yonas was sad and gave him your giraffe. That was kind."

Abebe beamed. A minute later he took the giraffe back, and Sofia let it go.

qa.q: What toy did Abebe give Yonas?
qa.a: Abebe gave Yonas his toy giraffe.

qa.q: What does Abebe's pat on Yonas's head suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Abebe felt caring and concerned, an early sign of empathy for his crying brother.

qa.q: Why was Sofia's response a wise one?
qa.a: Sofia noticed the kind act and named it warmly, and didn't demand Abebe keep sharing when he took the giraffe back.

qa.q: How might Yonas experience his brother's gesture?
qa.a: Yonas may feel comforted by the toy and the pat, and calmer as he stops crying.

grounding: Shows an older toddler comforting a crying baby with a toy, and a parent who warmly names it without demanding it every time.

passage:
Tuesday. Baby Ravi cried. Manoj, two, covered his ears and walked away.

Friday. Ravi cried again. Manoj brought him a spoon and patted him. Minakshi said softly, "You helped Ravi. That was kind."

Two weeks later. Ravi cried at bath time. Manoj brought the rubber duck and said, "Duck, baby." The next evening he ignored the crying and kept playing. Minakshi didn't mind.

qa.q: What did Manoj bring Ravi at bath time?
What was Manoj feeling when he patted Ravi on Friday?
qa.a: Manoj felt caring and concerned for his crying brother, showing early empathy.

qa.q: Why was it wise for Minakshi not to mind when Manoj ignored the crying?
qa.a: Empathy grows naturally when it is noticed and named, not demanded every time.

qa.q: How might Ravi feel when Manoj brings the duck?
qa.a: Ravi may feel soothed and comforted by his brother's attention and the duck.

grounding: Shows an older toddler's early empathy towards a crying baby, noticed and named warmly by a parent without demanding it every time.
